scope_note: SG-CS-PRESCRIPTION-SPECIAL-RULES after corrections following the V10D audit. The Massachusetts layer over 21 CFR 1306.07(b) is now taught: M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 9(b) limits a practitioner's dispensing to what immediate treatment needs until a pharmacy can fill a prescription, and 105 CMR 700.010(A) bars a practitioner from dispensing to a patient except as samples (immediate administration is not barred; under 105 CMR 700.001 a sample is in the manufacturer's package and not repackaged), so worked example 5 resolves a counted-out take-home supply as unavailable in Massachusetts. decision_logic[6] separates splitting a prescription from a patient-requested partial fill (21 CFR 1306.13(b); M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 18(d3/4) on request); decision_logic[16] applies the 90-day ceiling to Schedule III only; the 30-day validity references note the five-day window for out-of-state prescriptions; the acetaminophen-codeine example is tablets. New rules: MA-PRACTITIONER-DISPENSING-IMMEDIATE-TREATMENT and MA-PRACTITIONER-DISPENSING-SAMPLES-ONLY; MA-OUTSTATE-CII-FILL-WINDOW, FED-CII-PARTIAL-PATIENT and MA-CII-PARTIAL-FILL-PATHWAY-LIMITS are now cited. Scope gate: all four actionable signals declined; FED-OUD-OTP and MA-CS-QUANTITY-II-III are the records this section already replaced, and MA-DPH-REGISTRANT-SCOPE and MA-PMP-STATUTORY-FRAMEWORK are neighbours of the 105 CMR 700.001 citation outside the declared scope.
